definitions.explanation: Behavior that appears unnatural, nervous, or suspicious. Used both in serious contexts (police reports, security) and casually to describe someone who looks nervous or guilty.

examples.japanese: {挙動|きょどう}{不審|ふしん}な⟦{人物|じんぶつ}→人物：03356_jinbutsu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}かけた→見かける：01644_mikakeru⟧。
examples.english: I spotted a person acting suspiciously.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{質問|しつもん}される→質問する：05637_shitsumonsuru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{挙動|きょどう}{不審|ふしん}になった。
examples.english: He started acting suspiciously when questioned.

examples.japanese: {挙動|きょどう}{不審|ふしん}な⟦{男|おとこ}→男：00561_otoko⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{店|みせ}→店：00497_mise⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{前|まえ}→前：02255_mae⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦うろうろ→うろうろ：05168_urouro⟧⟦していた→する：00392_suru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、⟦{警察|けいさつ}→警察：01393_keisatsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{通報|つうほう}→通報：14318_tsuuhou⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: A man was acting suspiciously, loitering in front of the store, so I called the police.

notes:
USAGE:
Used in police and security contexts for describing suspicious persons, but also used casually and humorously. The shortened slang form ⟦{挙動|きょどう}→挙動：16126_kyodou⟧る (kyodoru) means "to act nervously/suspiciously" in informal speech.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {挙動|きょどう}{不審|ふしん}な⟦{人物|じんぶつ}→人物：03356_jinbutsu⟧ (suspicious person)
- {挙動|きょどう}{不審|ふしん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧ (to start acting suspiciously)
- {挙動|きょどう}{不審|ふしん}で⟦{職務質問|しょくむしつもん}→職務質問：15010_shokumushitsumon⟧⟦される→する：00392_suru⟧ (to be stopped and questioned for suspicious behavior)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{不審者|ふしんしゃ}→不審者：11348_fushinsha⟧: suspicious person — focuses on the person rather than the behavior
- ⟦{怪|あや}しい→怪しい：10267_ayashii⟧: suspicious, fishy — a broader, more casual adjective
